sections.content: Use ya with the *pretérito* *perfecto* to say that something has already happened or has already been done. Ya normally appears before the participle or after the auxiliary: Ya he *preparado* la *cena*. In invitation contexts, it can explain that you have already made plans or preparations.

items.english: I have already made a plan.
We have already accepted the invitation.

sections.content: ya can even stand alone as a one-word answer: to ¿Ya has *cenado*?, a simple 'Ya' means 'already done' — Spanish speakers use it as shorthand far more often than English uses a bare 'already'.
